overall: The AG found the Ware Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law by holding a May 6 executive session on an improper Purpose 3 topic with an insufficiently specific notice, finding the violation intentional, referring for a hearing with a recommended $300 fine, and declining to nullify the votes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the May 6 executive session discussion of Baystate's proposal and Gilbert Trust funding was not a proper Purpose 3 litigation topic.
allegations.key_passage: As we have been presented with no information that litigation was threatened over Baystate’s plan to establish a convenient care center, we find that the Board met in executive session for an improper purpose.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the May 6 meeting notice did not list topics with sufficient specificity; the notice omitted Baystate and the Gilbert Trust.
allegations.key_passage: Upon reading the notice of the May 6 meeting, a reasonable member of the public would not understand the anticipated nature of the Board’s discussion.

allegations.summary: Complainant argued the violation was intentional; AG found the Board had been warned in OML 2020-53 and treated the violation as intentional.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board has been warned that failure to identify the subject of a Purpose 3 executive session discussion violates the Open Meeting Law, unless identifying the subject would compromise the lawful purpose for the executive session, we find the violation here intentional.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked the AG to nullify the May 6 and July 1 votes; the AG found nullification not disproportionate but declined to exercise discretion to nullify.
allegations.key_passage: After much consideration, however, we decline to exercise our discretion to nullify the votes.

remedy: Refer the matter for a hearing under 940 CMR 29.07(3) and recommend a $300 civil penalty for the intentional violation.
Order the Board's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent.
Amend the July 1 minutes to include the vote affirming the May 6 vote to work with Bank of America.
remedy_passage: we refer this matter for a hearing pursuant to 940 CMR 29.07(3) and recommend that the Board be assessed a fine of $300 pursuant to G.L. c. 30A, § 23(c)
